text:
Nothing in the specs says what rung 7 should do for a path that is another checkout of the registered package. The code refuses such a path as `name-taken`. The only part of this I did not re-read is `author/verify.py`, which the previous review confirmed at lines 186-199.

- **SCF-B18** (`blueprint-and-scaffold.spec.md:115`) names rung 7 only as `workflows register <path> --check`, then `register`. It says nothing about a second checkout.
- **UPD-B24** (`engine-update.spec.md:155`) already specifies `name-taken` for `workflows register`. It is refused when the name, or its private import name, is registered from another path. It has no notion of "another checkout of the same package", so a second checkout falls under the refusal.
- **Reconcile rule:** `engine-update.spec.md:122-124` is a second `name-taken` rule. It covers a cached plugin whose name is already registered from a local path.
- **Code (read):** `registry.py:138-141` raises `name-taken` when the name or private name matches and `Path(entry.path).resolve() != root`. It has no same-package identity test.
- **Code (read):** `registry.py:142-148` rewrites the entry with `path=root`. A passing second checkout would therefore repoint the entry unless the rule changes.
- **Tests:** `test_registry.py:79-84` asserts `name-taken` for a different package at another path. `test_install.py:255` asserts it for reconcile. No test covers a second checkout.

ARTIFACT gap_finding: No spec states a rule for a second checkout. SCF-B18 (blueprint-and-scaffold.spec.md:115) names rung 7 only as "workflows register <path> --check, then register" (UPD-B20). UPD-B24 (engine-update.spec.md:155) already specifies name-taken for `workflows register` (name or private import name registered from another path), with no notion of "another checkout of the same package"; engine-update.spec.md:122-124 is a second name-taken rule (reconcile of cached plugins). Code (read): author/verify.py:186-199 `_register` calls reg.register(check_only=True) then reg.register(root, caps), turns a RegistryRefusal into a finding with its code. package/registry.py:138-141 raises name-taken when name or private_name matches and Path(entry.path).resolve() != root, so a linked worktree of the same package is refused today; there is no same-package identity test. registry.py:142-148 rewrites the entry with path=root, so a pass would repoint the entry and rung 7 writes the registry on every run. Tests: test_registry.py:79-84 (tested) asserts name-taken for a different package at another path and in-place re-register at the same path; test_install.py:255 asserts name-taken in reconcile; no test covers a second checkout or rung 7 in a worktree. Missing: a behaviour, scenarios and criterion for a second checkout (pass or skip without a second home, entry unchanged) beside a still-refused different package, and how "same package" is identified.
